set.approach: The trailhead lies where the Illecillewaet Campground road finishes, just off the Trans-Canada Highway near Rogers Pass. The Sir Donald trail climbs into the basin below the Vaux Glacier, then crosses Vaux Creek above the waterfall and skirts the base of a steep moraine to a lower bivy site. From there, follow the moraine crest to a short gully on the left and cross slopes under the west face to the Uto-Sir Donald col, which doubles as a high bivy. The Northwest Ridge starts from this col. A wilderness pass is needed for backcountry camping, and snow on the slopes below the col may call for an ice axe and crampons early in the season.
set.descent_text: The standard descent follows the Northwest Ridge back down, using bolted two-bolt rappel stations spaced for a 50 m rope, with downclimbing between them where the ridge eases. Note the first station on the way up: it marks where to leave the crest. Lower stations leave the ridge and drop the west face, with offset anchors to limit rockfall when pulling ropes. Below the last of the face stations, scree and ledges lead to slab or snow at the base of a dihedral, then two more rappels or 4th-class downclimbing reach the scree trail back to the Uto-Sir Donald col. When dry, a bypass from the summit follows the south ridge briefly, then traverses west-face ledges back to the Northwest Ridge. Falling rock from other parties is the main hazard, so wear a helmet and check every anchor, since old slings remain beside the bolts.

review.notes: Official Parks Canada descent guide for the NW Ridge: approach to col, station sequence, bypass. Counts and distances deliberately left out (single source).

set.approach: Start at the Illecillewaet Campground trailhead and follow the Sir Donald trail into the basin below the Vaux Glacier, then cross Vaux Creek above the waterfall. Continue by moraine and the slopes below the west face to the Uto-Sir Donald col, the high bivy site. The Southwest Ridge of Uto begins from the col, in the same terrain as the start of Sir Donald's Northwest Ridge. Early in the season, snow on the slope to the col can need an ice axe and crampons.
set.descent_text: One way down is to cross the summit and drop Uto's Northwest Ridge, which involves one steep rappel followed by loose, somewhat exposed third-class scrambling to a low saddle above the col. Early-season snow and icy patches on the way down call for an ice axe.

review.notes: Misfiled: this is Uto Peak, not Sir Donald. Parks Canada gives the col approach; advcollective gives route starts at the col; sverdina gives the NW-ridge descent.

set.approach: Walk up from the Hermit parking area to Hermit Meadows, then follow cairns and a faint beaten path through meadows and past waterfalls to a low point on the west ridge above the Tupper glacier, the Tupper shoulder. The route starts here, where the path gives way to boulder scrambling along the ridge.
set.descent_text: Descend the route. Bolted rappel anchors are found under the summit block, above the main corner crack, and beneath and left of the large Hermit gendarme, with extra slung blocks along the ridge. Memorise where each sits while climbing, since they hide easily from above. Rappelling or downclimbing the loose steps are both options.

review.notes: Both pages: approach via Hermit Meadows to the shoulder; descend by retracing with rappel anchors.

set.approach: The usual approach goes up Nesakwatch Creek: a rough, high-clearance forest road leads to a trailhead, followed by a short, steep and strenuous trail to the base of the climb. The ridge is mainly scrambling with a few fifth-class sections, and no glacier travel is needed.
set.descent_text: The Northeast Ridge is used to descend. It alternates between snow and rock, with krummholz to push through and a few short rappels, and it ends in a basin on the Centre Creek side, well away from the Nesakwatch approach.

review.notes: Approach: two pages agree on a steep Nesakwatch Creek trail. Descent from one trip report, testimony removed.

set.approach: Walk the Elk River trail from the signed trailhead on Highway 28 up to Landslide Lake, then continue to the col at the north end of the massif. The climb goes straight up Evacuation Gully, between the North Tower and the Northwest Summit, to reach the summit ridge.
set.descent_text: The ridge is followed south over the Northwest and Northeast peaks to the Main Summit. To get off, walk back over the ridge to the low, deep notch separating the Northeast and Northwest peaks, then descend the gully on the west face, then contour around under the west face to return to the north col.

review.notes: Route page: Evacuation Gully start and ridge descent; area page: trailhead and Elk River trail to Landslide Lake.
